advice: Experiment: fuse `sme_transpose` and `sme_gemm` into one SME helper marked `target("sme")`, `__arm_new("za")`, and `__arm_locally_streaming`. Keep the existing transpose layout, multiplication tile order, four ZA MOPA selectors, and FP32 arithmetic unchanged; perform scratch allocation and free inside `gemm`. This removes one streaming-region exit and re-entry between transpose and multiplication. Hypothesis: fewer SME mode transitions may reduce complete-call time. Measure the full `gemm` call, including allocation, transpose, multiplication, and free, against fresh AC controls. This is unverified advice, not a performance claim.
risks: The compiler may already reduce transition overhead, so the change may not help. A combined region may increase live ZA state or make code generation worse. Check compilation and ABI boundaries, correctness at tolerance 0.002 for n=512 and odd/tail sizes, n<=0 behavior, and repeated complete-call measurements. Preserve the fixed benchmark and controls; do not attribute a joint outcome to this experiment alone if it is measured with others.
